public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 197

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/197](https://www.erdosproblems.com/197)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set

namespace Erdos197

/--
Can $\mathbb{N}$ be partitioned into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid monotone
3-term arithmetic progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_197 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A B : Set ℕ, IsCompl A B ∧
      (∃ f : ℕ ≃ A, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ f) 3) ∧
      (∃ g : ℕ ≃ B, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ g) 3) := by
  sorry

end Erdos197

reformulations.difference: Lean uses nonnegative naturals and requires both parts to admit bijections from ℕ. Adenwalla's Question 6 asks about positive integers and does not separately require the two parts to be infinite.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Translating every value by one transports partitions of nonnegative integers to partitions of positive integers and preserves arithmetic progressions. Requiring infinite parts also loses no possible solution: if one part were finite, the other would contain every integer above some N. In any enumeration of that cofinite part, let a be the first value at least N and b the first value greater than a. Their indices are increasing, and 2b−a>b belongs to the part and must appear after b, producing a monotone 3-term AP. Hence both parts of any successful partition must be infinite, and every infinite subset of ℕ admits a bijection from ℕ. Translation invariance and the cofinite obstruction were proved in the scratch file, though the complete partition-level equivalence was not formalized.

sources_consulted: Sarosh Adenwalla, Avoiding Monotone Arithmetic Progressions in Permutations of Integers, arXiv:2211.04451v7 (2024), Introduction and Question 6 with its subsequent remarks; LaTeX source obtained from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2211.04451
Mathlib/Order/Disjoint.lean, definitions and lemmas for IsCompl
review.notes: No mathematical defect found in the sole declaration. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean establish that HasMonotoneAP f 3 is equivalent to the existence of indices i < j < k with f i + f k = 2 * f j. The equivalences used in the declaration ensure injectivity, excluding constant progressions. Both increasing and decreasing progressions are recognized; non-monotone arrangements and empty witnesses were checked. IsCompl gives exactly a disjoint cover, and the answer slot has the correct scope and affirmative polarity. Source-access limitation: erdosproblems.com/197 returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its current text and remarks could not be read directly. The mathematical question was independently checked against Adenwalla's explicit Question 6; the current community database still records problem 197 as open, consistent with the file.
